title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-evaluate.ts, make exactly ONE single-line edit. Do not make any
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-evaluate.ts, make exactly ONE single-line edit. Do not make any other change.

The exact line
          : await runCheck(bunCmd, ["test"], baseForDelta, "bun test (baseline)", SUITE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS);
occurs exactly once in the file (verified with rg -F -c: 1 match). Replace only its third argument, so the line becomes exactly:
          : await runCheck(bunCmd, ["test"], await buildOverlay(baseForDelta, baseForDelta, stagedFiles), "bun test (baseline)", SUITE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS);

Everything else on that line stays byte-identical. buildOverlay and stagedFiles are already in scope in this module — buildOverlay is declared in this same file (async function buildOverlay(baseRoot, mitosisRoot, stagedFiles)) and stagedFiles is the same variable already passed to the patched-side call `runRoot = await buildOverlay(baseRootForOverlay, mitosisRoot, stagedFiles);`. No new import is needed. Do not add a new variable or a new statement; make the change inline on that one line.

WHY THIS IS CORRECT: buildOverlay copies each staged file from its SECOND argument. Passing baseForDelta as both the base and the mitosis root therefore produces an overlay identical in STRUCTURE to the patched overlay but identical in CONTENT to the base tree.

THE DEFECT THIS FIXES: the patched suite already runs inside a symlink overlay, while the baseline suite runs directly against the real base tree. Any test whose result depends on the tree's physical shape therefore differs between the two runs for reasons unrelated to the diff, and the delta reports it as INTRODUCED BY THE PATCH. Measured three separate times today against repos/activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts: src/routes/trace-key-agreement.test.ts Glob-scans its sibling tree and asserts expect(sources.length).toBeGreaterThan(50), a guard its own comment describes as "guards the scan itself". Inside the overlay, non-test sources are symlinks and Bun's Glob.scan does not traverse symlinks (measured directly: 1 visible .ts file versus 212 reachable via find -L), so the corpus is empty and the guard fires correctly — it is detecting that it is blind. On the real base tree the same test passes, so the delta calls it new. Each of the three refused patches was independently verified correct: clean `bun run typecheck` and 4 pass / 0 fail for that exact test on a clean copy of the vessel. Two of them had to be landed by an operator by hand as a result. After this change the baseline and patched runs are structurally identical, so an overlay artifact fails on BOTH sides and cancels out of the delta.

Do NOT modify buildOverlay itself. Do NOT modify the patched-side call. Do NOT touch the failure-name parsing, the truncation guard, or any fail-closed branch — each guards a documented past regression.
